narratives.Description: scope:complete refuses a story whose acceptance clauses have no green command even when an operator has recorded a disposition for them, and its refusal does not name the clauses that are the gap. The acceptance-disposition grant records only `deferred`, and no verb moves a sentence that is not a criterion out of the way, so workers hand-edit the acceptance block and recompute its digest. This story builds the accepted design (synthesis 6969950740, Bound lean 6969795502): three grant values, a walk that leaves this run's granted clauses out of its counts, a refusal that names the unresolved clauses, and one `scope:confess` verb.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator completing a story, I want a clause I dropped or waived to count as handled, and a sentence that is not a criterion to be confessed by a verb, so that completion no longer needs a hand-edited acceptance block, a recomputed digest, or a confession PR.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/policy/acceptance-disposition-grant.ts: store the disposition value on the grant (new surface), default `deferred` for old grants; viewOf accepts a missing deferred-to for `not_applicable` and `waived`; acceptanceDispositionRecordFor writes the stored value and `deferred_to` only for `deferred`; formatAcceptanceDispositionCommand names `--disposition` and `--deferred-to` only for `deferred`; applyAcceptanceDispositionGrants also returns the clause ids it stamped this run with value and reason.
2. packages/runtime/src/authz.ts: `--disposition` flag, `--deferred-to` required for `deferred` and refused otherwise, `--reason` required, `authz:show` prints the value.
3. packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts: pass the granted clauses of this run to the completion walk.
4. packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts and acceptance-resolver.ts: the clause walk leaves granted clauses out of walked, failed, adjudicableUnverified and verified, prints each as granted, and the printed lead names the granted count.
5. packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts: the completion zero-verified rule is decided from the counts; the refusal lists each clause that is neither verified nor granted with the two remedies.
6. New packages/core/src/scope/confess.ts plus main.ts, index.ts, route-argv.ts, tasks/scope.yml and commands.md: `scope:confess --sentence` / `--all-unmapped`.
7. Tests for each, one changelog fragment.
narratives.Overview:
1. Grant values. `authz:grant --template acceptance-disposition` takes `--disposition deferred|not_applicable|waived`; the default is `deferred`, so today's calls are unchanged. `--reason` is required for every value. `--deferred-to` is required for `deferred` and refused for the other two. The value is stored on the grant beside the existing deferred-to and reason fields; a grant minted before this change reads as `deferred`. `acceptanceDispositionRecordFor` writes the grant's value, and writes `deferred_to` only for `deferred`. The grant reader (`viewOf`) accepts a grant with no deferred-to value when its stored value is `not_applicable` or `waived`, and still requires deferred-to when the stored value is `deferred` or absent. The resolve step, the apply step and the restamp check of a completed brief (`checkCitedAcceptanceDispositionGrants`) all use that reader, so a new-value grant is stamped, enters the granted set and restamps from `acceptanceDispositionRecordFor`. The remint text (`formatAcceptanceDispositionCommand`) names `--disposition <value>` and names `--deferred-to` only for `deferred`. `authz:show` prints the stored value. The mint gate, the clause-text digest, expiry and the place of the apply step in complete prep are unchanged.
2. Granted set. `applyAcceptanceDispositionGrants` already returns the ids it stamped in this run. `scope:complete` passes the clause ids among them to its walk as the granted set. Nothing else enters that set: a disposition written into the brief, with or without a grant id, does not.
3. Walk counts. In the `scope:complete` walk, a clause in the granted set is not counted in `walked`, `failed`, `adjudicableUnverified` or the verified count, and the walk prints it as granted with its value and reason. The printed lead is built after this omission and names the granted count. The zero-verified rule at completion is decided from these counts, not from the printed text: it refuses only when at least one clause is neither verified nor granted, no clause is verified and no executable command ran green. A walk whose every clause is granted, or verified or granted, passes without a command. The clause stays in `acceptance.clauses`; the sentence floor and the admitted-source identity check read the brief as today.
4. Refusal text. When the completion walk refuses, it lists each clause id that is neither verified nor granted, with the start of its text, and gives two remedies: a verify command that covers the clause, or the grant command with that clause id and a value. This replaces the "(disposition is not a substitute)" sentence on that refusal.
5. Non-criterion clause. A clause that is not a criterion is marked by the item 1 grant with `not_applicable` and a reason. The brief, its clauses, sentences, pin and digest are not edited.
6. Non-criterion sentence. `deft scope:confess -- <brief> --sentence "<text>"` (repeatable) or `--all-unmapped` appends to `acceptance.confessions` each named sentence that is in `acceptance.sentences`, is not a clause text and is not an admitted-source identity. It prints each sentence it wrote and changes nothing else in the brief. It refuses, and writes nothing, for a sentence that is not in the list, or that is an admitted-source identity; for the second it names the item 1 grant for that sentence's clause.
7. `verify:ac` run outside `scope:complete`, the rapid check, the evidence gate and the merge stamper are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an `acceptance-disposition` grant minted with `--disposition not_applicable --reason R` on clause 5, when `scope:complete` runs, then clause 5's plan item carries `not_applicable`, reason R and the grant id, and no merge evidence.
- Given `--disposition waived` with `--deferred-to 7`, then the mint refuses and names the flag; given `--disposition deferred` without `--deferred-to`, then the mint refuses as today.
- Given a grant minted before this change, when `scope:complete` applies it, then the item carries `deferred` and its `deferred_to`.
- Given a `waived` grant on clause 12 of a brief that `scope:complete` completed, when the completed brief is restamped, then the restamp check finds the grant and the item keeps `waived` with the grant id.
- Given a `not_applicable` grant whose clause text has changed, when `scope:complete` refuses, then the remint text names `--disposition not_applicable` and does not name `--deferred-to`.
- Given a stored grant with value `deferred` and no deferred-to value, when it is read, then it is treated as malformed as today.
- Given a brief with no verify command whose every clause is covered by a grant applied in this run, when `scope:complete` runs, then the walk passes, the clauses are still in `acceptance.clauses` and the output lists each clause as granted.
- Given a brief with no verify command, two clauses granted and one clause neither verified nor granted, when `scope:complete` runs, then it refuses, names that clause id and prints both remedies.
- Given a clause-keyed item whose `x-directive/disposition` was written into the brief by hand, with a human-origin shape and a grant id, and no matching grant in the store, when `scope:complete` runs with no verify command, then the walk still refuses for that clause.
- Given a grant whose clause text has changed since mint, when `scope:complete` runs, then it refuses as today and no clause enters the granted set.
- Given a clause granted in this run that also has a token oracle that fails, when `scope:complete` runs, then that clause does not count as failed.
- Given an unmapped sentence that is not an admitted-source identity, when `scope:confess --sentence` names it, then it is appended to `acceptance.confessions`, nothing else in the brief changes and `verify:ac` no longer reports it as unmapped.
- Given a sentence that is an admitted-source identity, when `scope:confess` names it, then it refuses, writes nothing and names the grant command for its clause.
- Given `scope:confess --all-unmapped`, then it confesses exactly the sentences the sentence floor reports as unmapped that are not admitted-source identities, and prints each.
- Given `verify:ac` run on a brief outside `scope:complete`, then its result is the same as before this change.

## In plain English
When a story finishes, `scope:complete` checks its acceptance clauses in two ways: every clause needs evidence or an operator disposition, and the acceptance walk must report at least one verified clause or a green command. Three gaps make stories stuck or force hand edits. The walk does not read dispositions at all, so a clause the operator dropped or waived still blocks it, and the refusal does not say which clauses need what. The operator grant that records a disposition can only write `deferred`, although the brief format already accepts `not_applicable` and `waived`. And there is no sanctioned way to take a sentence that is not a criterion out of the brief: workers hand-edit the acceptance block and recompute its digest, which the integrity check was built to refuse. The recommended fix widens the existing grant to all three values, lets the walk skip clauses that carry a grant disposition, and adds one verb that re-reads the acceptance block from the issue body as it is now, so the operator fixes the issue text and the brief follows.

The issue has no `## Acceptance Criteria` heading. The three pains below are derived from its `## Expected` section, one per bullet.

## Pains
- P1 — The acceptance walk at completion does not accept a recorded disposition where no executable pass applies, and its refusal does not name which clauses need an executable pass or a disposition (#6602 clauses 5 and 12).
- P2 — The `acceptance-disposition` grant records only `deferred`; it cannot record `not_applicable` or `waived` with an operator reason.
- P3 — No verb removes a clause that is not a criterion; the only route is hand-editing the brief's acceptance block and recomputing the admitted-source digest (#6601, #6639).

## Constraints (not pains)
- No new gate, grant template, refusal or stored policy flag. Narrowing an existing check is allowed; adding one is not.
- An agent must not be able to drop a real criterion silently. The #5055 admitted-source identity check stays the guard for that.
- #6609 fixes what ingest harvests (in parallel; not this arc). #6645 fixes the story marks and the unreachable delivery-identity remedy (in parallel; not this arc). This arc must not depend on either landing first.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts` 78-80: `ACCEPTANCE_DISPOSITIONS = ["waived", "deferred", "not_applicable"]`. 636-700 `parseDisposition`: reason, recorded_at and a human-origin provenance shape are required. 1612-1650 `applyGrantedDispositions` stamps grant dispositions in memory. 1878-1886: the complete remedy text ends "(disposition is not a substitute)". 1898-2012 `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk`: refuses a zero-verified walk unless the predicate is `executable-pass`; merge provenance admits only clause-less historical briefs (#5403).
- `packages/core/src/check/rapid-zero-verified.ts` 108-120 `scopeCompleteRejectsZeroVerifiedWalk` (#4870).
- `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts` 905-986: complete prep order is persist clause-keyed items, apply disposition grants, merge stamp, evidence gate, then the walk.
- `packages/core/src/policy/acceptance-disposition-grant.ts` 1-18 (deferred only), 140-160 `--deferred-to` parse, 555-596 `applyAcceptanceDispositionGrants`.
- `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts` 1786-1872 `evaluateStatementSentenceCoverage`: a sentence must be a clause or a confession.
- `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts` 1656-1776 `resolveAdmittedSourceIdentities` (merge-base pin first, then working pin with a live REST digest compare), 1779-1886 `applyAdmittedSourceIdentityGate`: an admitted identity that is no longer a clause, or is only confessed, fails (#5055).
- No `deft` verb writes `acceptance.confessions` or rewrites `acceptance.clauses` after ingest (search of `packages/` at the pin).

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- F1. Three values on the existing grant (P2). `authz:grant --template acceptance-disposition` takes `--disposition deferred|not_applicable|waived` (default `deferred`, so today's calls are unchanged). `--reason` is required for every value; `--deferred-to` is required for `deferred` only and refused for the other two. Mint path, clause-text digest, expiry and the apply step in complete prep are unchanged.
- F2. The walk honours grant dispositions (P1). In `scope:complete`, a clause whose clause-keyed plan item carries a disposition applied from a grant in this run is left out of the walk: it is not adjudicated and does not count toward the zero-verified rule, the sentence floor or the admitted-source identity check. When every clause is either verified or so dispositioned, the walk passes without an executable command. A disposition written into the brief by hand does not get this exclusion. Merge provenance alone stays no substitute for an executable pass (#4870 unchanged).
- F3. The refusal names the clauses (P1). When the walk refuses, it lists each clause id that is neither verified nor dispositioned and gives the two remedies: a verify command that covers it, or the grant command with that clause id.
- F4. One refresh verb (P3). `deft scope:refresh-acceptance -- <brief>` re-reads the origin issue body at its current revision through the ingest harvest and rewrites `sentences`, `clauses`, `admitted_source_sentences` and `admitted_source_digest`. A clause whose text is unchanged keeps its id; new text gets new ids above the highest; the clause-keyed pending item of a removed clause is removed. It prints every removed and added clause. The operator removes a non-criterion by editing the issue text; nobody edits the brief or computes a digest.
- F5. The identity check follows the source (P3). When the working pin differs from the merge-base pin, `resolveAdmittedSourceIdentities` uses the working pin only if its digest equals the live digest of the origin issue body; otherwise (offline, or a mismatch) today's result stands and the message names `scope:refresh-acceptance`. Taking a granted clause out of the clause list would also make its own sentence unmapped and fail the identity check, so the story would stay stuck. The walk exclusion is safe only when it means the clause ids this completion's grant step stamped. The value is stored on the grant beside the existing deferred-to and reason fields; a grant minted before this change reads as `deferred`. `acceptanceDispositionRecordFor` writes the grant's value, and writes `deferred_to` only for `deferred`. The grant reader (`viewOf`) accepts a grant with no deferred-to value when its stored value is `not_applicable` or `waived`, and still requires deferred-to when the stored value is `deferred` or absent. The resolve step, the apply step and the restamp check of a completed brief (`checkCitedAcceptanceDispositionGrants`) all use that reader, so a new-value grant is stamped, enters the granted set and restamps from `acceptanceDispositionRecordFor`. The remint text (`formatAcceptanceDispositionCommand`) names `--disposition <value>` and names `--deferred-to` only for `deferred`. `authz:show` prints the stored value. The mint gate, the clause-text digest, expiry and the place of the apply step in complete prep are unchanged.

Granted set. `applyAcceptanceDispositionGrants` already returns the ids it stamped in this run. `scope:complete` passes the clause ids among them to its walk as the granted set. Nothing else enters that set: a disposition written into the brief, with or without a grant id, does not.

Walk counts. In the `scope:complete` walk, a clause in the granted set is not counted in `walked`, `failed`, `adjudicableUnverified` or the verified count, and the walk prints it as granted with its value and reason. The printed lead is built after this omission and names the granted count. The zero-verified rule at completion is decided from these counts, not from the printed text: it refuses only when at least one clause is neither verified nor granted, no clause is verified and no executable command ran green. A walk whose every clause is granted, or verified or granted, passes without a command. The clause stays in `acceptance.clauses`; the sentence floor and the admitted-source identity check read the brief as today.

Refusal text. When the completion walk refuses, it lists each clause id that is neither verified nor granted, with the start of its text, and gives two remedies: a verify command that covers the clause, or the grant command with that clause id and a value. This replaces the "(disposition is not a substitute)" sentence on that refusal.
Non-criterion clause. A clause that is not a criterion is marked by the item 1 grant with `not_applicable` and a reason. The brief, its clauses, sentences, pin and digest are not edited.

Non-criterion sentence. `deft scope:confess -- <brief> --sentence "<text>"` (repeatable) or `--all-unmapped` appends to `acceptance.confessions` each named sentence that is in `acceptance.sentences`, is not a clause text and is not an admitted-source identity. It prints each sentence it wrote and changes nothing else in the brief. It refuses, and writes nothing, for a sentence that is not in the list, or that is an admitted-source identity; for the second it names the item 1 grant for that sentence's clause.

Given a grant minted before this change, when `scope:complete` applies it, then the item carries `deferred` and its `deferred_to`.
